args.title: checkout-api health check failures after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 was deployed to all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and began failing health checks, with error rate at 18%. Rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production (deployment history: v2.2.9 healthy, v2.3.0 healthy, v2.3.1 unhealthy). Rollback completed and verified across all three regions; service is now healthy with error rate at ~0.2%. Note: v2.3.1-rc in staging is also unhealthy, which may indicate the defect originates earlier in the release candidate line. v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until the cause of the health check failures is identified and fixed.

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

**Diagnosis**
- `checkout-api` was running **v2.3.1** in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), failing health checks with an **18% error rate**.
- Deployment history: v2.2.9 (healthy) → v2.3.0 (healthy) → v2.3.1 (unhealthy). `v2.3.1-rc` is staging-only and also unhealthy, so it was not a valid rollback target.

**Action taken**
- Rolled back to **v2.3.0**, the most recent production-healthy release, across all production regions. Rollout verified.
- No change-manager approval was needed since v2.3.0 has previously been healthy in production.

**Verification**
- Service is now healthy: **v2.3.0** in all regions, error rate down to **0.2%**.

**Incident**
- Opened **INC-0001** (SEV2, on-call paged) describing the failed v2.3.1 deploy, the rollback to v2.3.0, and the current healthy state. I also flagged in the summary that `v2.3.1-rc` in staging is unhealthy too, suggesting the defect predates the production deploy — v2.3.1 shouldn't be redeployed until the root cause is fixed.

One follow-up worth considering: since the staging RC was also unhealthy, the release appears to have been promoted to production despite a bad staging signal — worth reviewing in the postmortem.
